title: Three holes in a full tank. Which jet lands farthest? The middle: 1.00 m. Top and bottom: 0.87 m.
description:
Three holes in a full tank. Which jet lands farthest? A tank of water 1 m deep stands on the floor and is kept full, so the level never drops. Three holes in its wall sit 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75 m below the surface. Each hole shoots a horizontal jet at the Torricelli speed sqrt(2 g h); the jets are drawn as streams of particles, one every 0.0125 s of simulated time, each in free fall (g = 9.80665 m/s^2, no air drag) until it reaches the floor. The landing distance of each jet is measured by stepping one particle at 3,600 steps per second and locating the floor crossing, then checked against the closed form 2 sqrt(h (H - h)). Deterministic, no seed. Played at one quarter speed.

Measured:
- top hole, 0.25 m down: exit speed 2.214 m/s, fall time 0.391 s, lands 0.866 m from the wall (closed form 0.866 m)
- middle hole, 0.50 m down: exit speed 3.132 m/s, fall time 0.319 s, lands 1.000 m from the wall (closed form 1.000 m)
- bottom hole, 0.75 m down: exit speed 3.835 m/s, fall time 0.226 s, lands 0.866 m from the wall (closed form 0.866 m)
- the middle jet wins by 13.4 cm; the top and bottom jets tie to 6e-8 m; the bottom jet leaves 1.732 times faster than the top jet but flies 1.732 times shorter
- closed forms: v = sqrt(2 g h), t = sqrt(2 (H - h) / g), range = 2 sqrt(h (H - h)); the range peaks at h = H / 2, where it equals H exactly; holes at h and H - h tie (0.1 and 0.9 m: 0.600 m; 0.4 and 0.6 m: 0.980 m)
- note (not drawn): if the tank were left to drain through one hole in its bottom, the level would fall as H (1 - t / T)^2 and the top half of the water would leave in 29.3 percent of the emptying time

Why: the water above a hole pushes on it, so a deeper hole makes a faster jet: the speed grows with the square root of the depth. But a lower hole is closer to the floor, so its jet has less height to fall through and less time in the air: the flight time grows with the square root of the height above the floor. The distance is speed times time, so it goes as the square root of depth times height. That product is largest when the depth and the height are equal, at the middle of the tank, and it is the same for any pair of holes that swap depth for height, so the top and bottom holes tie.

Rerun sims/torricelli/torricelli.py with projects/torricelli/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
